blocks.text: CSRF occurs when a browser sends ambient credentials with a cross-site request and the application accepts an unauthorized state change. CORS response readability is not required for a CSRF attack.

items: HTML forms and state-changing GET endpoints
Missing, reused or incorrectly session-bound CSRF tokens
Simple content types accepted by JSON endpoints
Origin/Referer validation and SameSite cookie behavior
Method overrides and double-submit cookie implementations

blocks.text: Use two controlled accounts and a separate test origin. Start with a harmless profile-preference change and verify persisted state in a fresh authenticated read. Run browser fixtures from the separate origin; a proxy replay does not establish that a browser will send the same cookies or headers. Check SameSite and third-party cookie behavior in the browser under test. Origin and Referer header fragments are proxy controls; JavaScript cannot freely set these forbidden headers.

Capture a valid request first, then omit or mutate its CSRF defenses individually. A missing token is a finding only when an unauthorized browser-triggered action succeeds. For double-submit cookies, separately assess whether an attacker can set the cookie used in the comparison. Never change recovery addresses, passwords or real payment details.

See `csrf-payloads.txt` for browser HTML fixtures, token mutations, content-type variants and request sequences. Adapt endpoint names and test account values; these are independent cases, not one HTML document or a universal wordlist.

files.name: csrf-payloads.txt

sections.label: Form-urlencoded POST: submit manually from the separate test origin
State-changing GET: requires endpoint support and browser cookies in the navigation context
Multipart form without files: test whether the same route accepts this simple content type
Simple fetch request: response may be unreadable, but independently inspect persisted test-account state
Token replacement fragments: use the actual parameter name, one case per request
Header-based defense negative controls: proxy mutations, not browser-settable arbitrary headers
SameSite matrix: repeat the harmless form with Strict, Lax and None; Secure test cookies.

files.content:
# CSRF Testing Payloads # Form-urlencoded POST: submit manually from the separate test origin
# State-changing GET: requires endpoint support and browser cookies in the navigation context Run GET preference test
# Multipart form without files: test whether the same route accepts this simple content type
# text/plain JSON-shaped form: produces {"displayName":"csrf-plain-marker","padding":"="}
# Simple fetch request: response may be unreadable, but independently inspect persisted test-account state fetch('https://app.example.test/profile/preferences',{method:'POST',credentials:'include',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'},body:'displayName=csrf-fetch-marker'}); fetch('https://app.example.test/profile/preferences',{method:'POST',credentials:'include',headers:{'Content-Type':'text/plain'},body:JSON.stringify({displayName:'csrf-text-marker'})}); # Token replacement fragments: use the actual parameter name, one case per request csrf_token= csrf_token=csrf-invalid-marker csrf_token=null csrf_token[]=csrf-array-marker csrf_token=csrf-first-marker&csrf_token=csrf-second-marker csrf_token=LAB_OTHER_SESSION_CSRF_TOKEN # Header-based defense negative controls: proxy mutations, not browser-settable arbitrary headers X-CSRF-Token: csrf-invalid-header-marker X-XSRF-Token: csrf-other-session-marker Origin: https://csrf-origin.example.test Origin: https://app.example.test.csrf-origin.example.test Referer: https://csrf-origin.example.test/form _method=PATCH&displayName=csrf-method-patch _method=PUT&displayName=csrf-method-put
Cookie: csrf_lab=csrf-cookie-marker csrf_lab=csrf-cookie-marker&displayName=csrf-double-submit-marker # SameSite matrix: repeat the harmless form with Strict, Lax and None; Secure test cookies. Set-Cookie: csrf_session=LAB_STRICT_COOKIE; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict Set-Cookie: csrf_session=LAB_LAX_COOKIE; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax Set-Cookie: csrf_session=LAB_NONE_COOKIE; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None
